Header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Time: 10:00 AM - 11:02 AM PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel, Marcus Liu, Jordan Reyes, Lina Gomez, Evan Park, Kara D'Souza + various squad leads (listed above)

[00:00] Sofia Patel: Alright, okay good morning everyone, thanks for making time. we'll run through a tight agenda — incident readout, squad shuffles, hiring implications, and customer comms. try to keep updates to five minutes.

[00:28] Marcus Liu: Quick note, I posted the slide deck in the channel — it's the one titled "Orbit Shift Q4 pivot". If anyone doesn't have access ping me.

[01:05] Jordan Reyes: I'm gonna start with the infra incident readout. TL;DR — our KV cache eviction policy interacted poorly with an unusual prefix distribution from a partner test, we hit cascading latency on some Dedicated nodes and the autoscaler misjudged warm pools.

[01:42] Lina Gomez: Can you restate that, jor- jordan? the cache eviction thing — was that a config drift or a code bug?

[02:10] Jordan Reyes: Mostly policy + telemetry gap. The policy change in late Sept to prefer memory compaction wasn't rolled out with the updated heuristics; so under the partner load we were thrashing. Not a kernel-level bug, more of a mismatch between tuning and observed sequence length distribution.

[02:55] Evan Park: We also saw that the warm pool tagging failed on three Dedicated clusters — the autoscaler thought nodes were healthy because GPU heartbeats were fine but the inference runtime had stalled on a few threads. That delay cascaded into the load balancer re-routing which spiked latency.

[03:30] Kara D'Souza: On the customer side we had two enterprise accounts open tickets — both from dedicated customers, they were impacted in the 95th-percentile latency window. CS triaged immediately, but we need a customer comms playbook so product doesn't have to craft on the spot.

[04:02] Marcus Liu: Understood. For the playbook, we'll standardize a 3-message cadence: acknowledgement, technical summary, remediation timeline. Kara can own the template.

[04:40] Sofia Patel: Good. Jordan, can you give us the detection and mitigation timeline for the incident? When did alerting trigger versus when we started mitigation?

[05:10] Jordan Reyes: Alert fired ~09:03 UTC, initial mitigation — rolling restart on the affected hosts at 09:10, then we disabled the compaction policy at 09:18, the autoscaler manual override at 09:25. By 09:40 latency was back under SLO for most routes. There's a residual 5-8% error increase on long-sequence generations we are investigating.

[05:48] Lina Gomez: We should capture those manual steps in runbooks — if the SE or oncall has to remember offsets that's risk.

[06:22] Evan Park: Agreed, I'll own the runbook update and also add a synthetic test that'll exercise the prefix distribution we saw. We'll schedule it to run during staging every night so we catch regressions.

[06:58] Sofia Patel: Great. Switching gears — squad rebalancing. Marcus?

[07:20] Marcus Liu: Ok, quick context: given the incident and a set of enterprise prospects that require Dedicated guarantees, we need to move two engineers from Model Onboarding to Infra SRE for 8 weeks and pull one product PM onto the onboarding roadmap to accelerate quantization recommendations. This is a net negative for throughput in onboarding but lowers enterprise risk.

[08:00] Lina Gomez: Which squads specifically? We need to coordinate with managers so sprint commitments are adjusted.

[08:18] Marcus Liu: Joey and Priya would move to Infra SRE. PM is Anita. We'll have proposals in the HR channel after this meeting.

[08:40] Jordan Reyes: From a technical perspective that helps. Having two folks on-site in infra SRE reduces our mean time to remediate for Dedicated incidents by an estimated 30-40 percent based on past cycles.

[09:05] Sofia Patel: Okay, I want a clear communication plan to the affected squads — not just a note, but a short sync and updated sprint plans. Lina, can you coordinate?

[09:32] Lina Gomez: Yep, I'll run a 15-minute swivel with the managers after this meeting and update the sprint board.

[10:01] Kara D'Souza: On customers — we prepared a pre-draft for the two impacted customers. Main ask is to include an engineering timeline and an offer for a dedicated postmortem call. We should also consider a small credit as a gesture; legal flagged the contract language and allowed a goodwill credit under 0.5% for incidents of this class.

[10:45] Marcus Liu: We need to be careful with credits — we shouldn't set a precedent. Kara, run it by Legal, but let's be measured.

[11:12] Sofia Patel: Good point. Now hiring: quick status on open roles and shifts because of the reallocation. HR note — Q4 hiring will focus on infra critical roles and one senior quantization engineer. Marcus?

[11:33] Marcus Liu: Recruiting is pushing five candidates for infra SRE; two onsites scheduled next week. For quantization we'll convert an IC+ hire to a senior role to shorten ramp. The cost delta is higher but ramp is faster.

[12:05] Lina Gomez: We also need to budget for ramp overlap — when we pull Joey and Priya back they'll need two weeks of re-onboarding. That should be in the hiring plan.

[12:30] Jordan Reyes: on Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs — several RFPs are requesting VPC-delivered Private deployments but also want burst capacity. We need a product decision on whether we offer a managed burst across regions for Private customers. The infra overhead is non-trivial.

[13:04] Evan Park: Technical note: managed cross-region burst requires consistent KV cache semantics across sites; our current cache invalidation model is eventually consistent and will cause token mismatches if we naively shard. So it's doable but we need to either accept tail latencies or design a global control plane for cache coherence.

[13:40] Kara D'Souza: Customers asking for both thin-hosted and private options because of data residency and cost concerns. We'll prioritize based on contract size and legal requirements.

[14:05] Sofia Patel: We should be explicit in sales materials about tradeoffs. Marcus, can the product marketing team include a simple matrix for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private?

[14:25] Marcus Liu: On it, will have a draft by EOD Friday.

[14:40] Speaker 3: —(mumble) — there's a question about SLA credits structure for multi-region deployments?

[15:05] Sofia Patel: Make a note — we need a standard SLA matrix for multi-region and single-region; legal and finance to sign. Kara and Evan will coordinate.

[15:32] Jordan Reyes: Back to the incident — we're going to run a model-mix stress test this coming Tuesday at 03:00 UTC to validate the compaction policy updates. Evan, will infra support that window?

[16:00] Evan Park: Yes, infra will support. We'll also enable verbose tracing for the runtime; that will produce a lot of logs so please warn observability.

[16:30] Marcus Liu: Observability — quick note, the traces didn't correlate cleanly with the autoscaler in the last incident. We need a better tag mapping (route→model→pool). I'll task the telemetry squad to add those dimensions.

[17:02] Lina Gomez: Also let's not forget on-call rotations, we had a gap two weekends ago — need to verify that schedule and ensure backups are clear.

[17:30] Kara D'Souza: CS will draft a proactive outreach playbook and include a template for the postmortem invite. We'll make sure it's customer-friendly and doesn't leak internal runbook steps.

[18:05] Sofia Patel: Great. Questions from the org: any blockers you want me to escalate?

[18:20] Speaker 4 (Squad Lead): We need a decision on whether to pause a non-critical initiative to free up a senior engineer. ETA on that decision?

[18:45] Sofia Patel: I'll arbitrate — send me the short tradeoff doc by EOD and I'll decide tomorrow morning.

[19:10] Marcus Liu: Finance note — redistributing headcount will change our run rate; we need to update forecasts before the mid-Oct board deck. I'll work with Fiona in Finance to model the 8-week shift.

[19:35] Jordan Reyes: One more technical ask — can product PMs include a short CPU/GPU utilization target in their tickets? Right now infra has to way overprovision because of vague workload descriptions.

[19:58] Marcus Liu: Good call, we'll add a template field for expected seq length distribution and expected concurrency so infra can make smarter autoscaling decisions.

[20:30] Sofia Patel: Alright let's go rapid-fire checkouts — two minute round, highlights and lowlights. Marcus start.

[20:40] Marcus Liu: Highlight: model catalog refresh shipped; Lowlight: the incident exposed telemetry gaps.

[21:15] Jordan Reyes: Highlight: runtime perf patch queued; Lowlight: the autoscaler misclassifies warm nodes.

[21:50] Lina Gomez: Highlight: manager alignment meeting scheduled; Lowlight: sprint drift on onboarding.

[22:20] Evan Park: Highlight: infra synthetic tests added; Lowlight: we need more headcount in SRE.

[22:50] Kara D'Souza: Highlight: customer triage went smoothly; Lowlight: customers expect faster remediation and clearer comms.

[23:10] Sofia Patel: Wrap-up — we have three immediate asks: 1) Incident postmortem doc to be circulated by Kara/Eng (due 2026-10-04); 2) Run scheduled stress test Tuesday (Infra + Eng) and share logs; 3) Squad realignment communication by Lina (update sprint board and run a short sync). Any objections?

[23:40] Marcus Liu: No objections.

[24:00] Speaker 5: Quick micro point — can we have a lightweight hotline for oncall to reach leadership if an incident is escalating? Last time emails were slow.

[24:20] Sofia Patel: Yes, we'll stand up a pager escalation path — Lina and Joanna from Ops will configure.

[24:50] Jordan Reyes: Also I want to call out that we should run a dry-run for the customer postmortem workflow so CS, Legal and Eng know roles.

[25:15] Kara D'Souza: We'll do a tabletop next week.

[25:40] Sofia Patel: Good. Any final questions?

[26:00] Marcus Liu: One last ask — is the board deck going to include this incident as a risk item?

[26:20] Sofia Patel: Yes, a short section on incident response and mitigation plans. Marcus will own the wording with FP.

[26:45] — (general agreement / murmurs) —

[27:10] Sofia Patel: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: expect the postmortem and customer comms drafts in the next 48 hours. Lina — run the manager sync. Kara — prepare customer outreach. Evan — tests. Jordan & Marcus — telemetry and runbook items. We'll reconvene as needed.

[27:45] Meeting ended at 11:02 AM PT.
